questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Berubari Union case, the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution.
2. In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
3. The Preamble has been amended more than once since 1950.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Berubari (1960) treated the Preamble as not part of the Constitution, but Kesavananda (1973) reversed this. The Preamble has been amended only once, by the 42nd Amendment (1976), which added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity'.

questions.q: Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, citizenship of India may be lost by all of the following modes EXCEPT
questions.e: The Act provides three modes of loss: renunciation (voluntary), termination (on voluntarily acquiring another country's citizenship) and deprivation (compulsory, by the Central Government). Expulsion is not a statutory mode.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The protections under Article 20 cannot be suspended during a National Emergency.
2. The protection against double jeopardy under Article 20(2) applies to proceedings before a court of law or a judicial tribunal.
3. Article 20(1) prohibits retrospective application of civil as well as criminal laws.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment bars suspension of Articles 20 and 21 during Emergency, and double jeopardy covers only judicial proceedings (not departmental action). Article 20(1) bars only ex post facto criminal laws; retrospective civil or tax laws are not covered.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Directive Principle : Article
1. Equal justice and free legal aid : Article 39A
2. Promotion of cooperative societies : Article 43B
3. Protection of monuments of national importance : Article 48A
4. Raising the level of nutrition and public health : Article 47
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Article 39A (42nd Amendment), 43B (97th Amendment) and 47 are correct. Article 48A deals with protection of environment, forests and wildlife; protection of monuments is Article 49.

questions.q:
Statement-I: A Constitution Amendment Bill cannot be passed through a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament if the Houses disagree on it.
Statement-II: The provision for a joint sitting under Article 108 applies only to ordinary bills and financial bills, not to money bills or Constitution Amendment Bills.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 368 requires a special majority in each House separately; Article 108 joint sitting is limited to ordinary and financial bills, so a deadlock on an amendment bill simply defeats it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the pardoning powers:
1. The Governor can grant pardon to a person sentenced to death under a State law.
2. Only the President can pardon sentences awarded by a court martial.
3. The Governor can commute a death sentence.
4. The President's pardoning power extends to death sentences.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 161 the Governor can suspend, remit or commute a death sentence but cannot pardon it; pardon of a death sentence and of court-martial sentences is a Presidential power under Article 72.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is correct?
o: The Speaker votes in the first instance in all divisions and also has a casting vote in a tie
The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a simple majority of members present and voting
The Speaker continues in office even after dissolution of the Lok Sabha until the new House meets
The Speaker is appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
questions.e: Under Article 94 the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution but until just before the first meeting of the next House. The Speaker votes only in a tie, removal needs an effective majority of all the then members, and the Speaker is elected by the House.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.
2. The writ jurisdiction of High Courts under Article 226 extends beyond enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
3. A High Court can issue writs only to authorities located within its own territory, with no exception based on where the cause of action arises.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 32 is the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution per Ambedkar, and Article 226 allows writs for 'any other purpose' too. Article 226(1), as widened by the 15th Amendment, lets a High Court act where the cause of action arises even if the authority is outside its territory.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct regarding Panchayati Raj under Part IX of the Constitution?
o: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats
Superintendence of Panchayat elections is vested in the State Election Commission
Elections to Panchayats are conducted by the Election Commission of India
A fresh election must be held within six months if a Panchayat is dissolved before expiry of its term
questions.e: Article 243K vests superintendence, direction and control of Panchayat elections in the State Election Commission, not the ECI. The other three statements are as per Articles 243G, 243K and 243E.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Eighth Schedule:
1. Sindhi was added by the 71st Amendment Act.
2. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment Act.
3. Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added by the 92nd Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sindhi was added earlier, by the 21st Amendment (1967). The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali, and the 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali, taking the total to 22.

questions.q: The Conrad discontinuity is generally regarded as the boundary between
o: the upper mantle and the lower mantle
the upper crust (sial) and the lower crust (sima)
the outer core and the inner core
questions.e: Conrad separates the upper and lower crust; the Mohorovicic discontinuity separates crust and mantle, the Gutenberg discontinuity the mantle and core, and the Lehmann discontinuity the outer and inner core.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Temperature increases with height in the stratosphere.
Statement-II: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Absorption of UV by ozone heats the upper stratosphere, so temperature rises with height, unlike the troposphere where it falls. This is why the stratosphere is stable and has little vertical mixing.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 8

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The subtropical westerly jet stream lies close to 30 degrees latitude in the upper troposphere.
2. The tropical easterly jet stream over peninsular India is associated with the summer monsoon.
3. Jet streams generally blow from east to west in the mid-latitudes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The westerly jet shifts north of the Himalayas in summer, while the tropical easterly jet over peninsular India is linked with the monsoon onset. Mid-latitude jets are westerly, not easterly.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 9; Class 11 India Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q: Which one of the following rivers is NOT a tributary of the Krishna?
questions.e: Manjra is a tributary of the Godavari. Bhima, Tungabhadra and Koyna all join the Krishna.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 India Physical Environment Ch 3; Majid Husain

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of local weather phenomenon and region is NOT correctly matched?
o: Blossom showers : Coffee-growing areas of Karnataka
questions.e: Loo is a hot, dry wind of the northern plains and northwest India in summer. The other three pre-monsoon phenomena are correctly matched.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 India Physical Environment Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Black soil is moisture retentive and develops deep cracks in the dry season.
2. Black soil is rich in lime, iron and magnesia but poor in nitrogen and organic matter.
3. Black soil is formed mainly from alluvium deposited by rivers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Black (regur) soil is formed from weathered basalt of the Deccan Trap, not river alluvium. Its high clay content gives moisture retention and the cracks that aerate it.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 India Physical Environment Ch 6

questions.q: Pneumatophores, or breathing roots, are most characteristic of which type of natural vegetation?
questions.e: Mangroves grow in waterlogged, saline, oxygen-poor mud, so roots grow upward to take in air. The Sundarbans, with Sundari trees, is the best known Indian example.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 India Physical Environment Ch 5

questions.q:
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the events given below?
1. Battle of Buxar
2. Treaty of Allahabad
3. Regulating Act
4. Pitt's India Act
questions.e: Buxar (1764) was followed by the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), which gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. Parliament then intervened with the Regulating Act (1773) and Pitt's India Act (1784).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Treaty of Srirangapatnam (1792) ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
2. The Nizam of Hyderabad was the first Indian ruler to accept the Subsidiary Alliance.
3. The Treaty of Bassein (1802) was signed with Peshwa Baji Rao II.
4. The Treaty of Salbai ended the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. The Treaty of Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War; the Second war (1803-05) ended with treaties such as Surji-Anjangaon and Deogaon.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lord William Bentinck:
1. He abolished the practice of sati by a Regulation passed in 1829.
2. During his tenure, the government resolved in 1835 to promote European literature and science through English as the medium of higher education.
3. He introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sati was abolished by Regulation XVII of 1829 and the Macaulay-backed resolution of 1835 made English the medium of higher education. The Doctrine of Lapse was Dalhousie's policy of the 1850s.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Movement : Associated feature
1. Santhal Hul (1855-56) : Led by Sido and Kanhu
2. Pabna revolt (1873-76) : Directed against indigo planters
3. Deccan riots (1875) : Directed against moneylenders
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Pabna agrarian leagues resisted zamindars' illegal enhancement of rent; the indigo revolt of 1859-60 was the movement against planters. The Santhal Hul and the Deccan riots are correctly matched.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a cause or grievance feeding into the Revolt of 1857?
o: Introduction of the Enfield rifle with greased cartridges
questions.e: The Vernacular Press Act came 21 years after the Revolt, as part of Lytton's reactionary policy. The other three heightened sepoy fear about caste, religion and overseas service.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Arya Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati in Bombay in 1875.
2. The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873.
3. The Prarthana Samaj was founded by Keshab Chandra Sen.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Prarthana Samaj (1867) was founded in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang, with M.G. Ranade later its guiding figure; Keshab Chandra Sen only inspired it. The other two statements are correct.

questions.q: Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress at its
questions.e: Besant presided at Calcutta in 1917 while the Home Rule agitation was at its height. Sarojini Naidu, who presided at Kanpur in 1925, was the first Indian woman President.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct regarding the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931?
o: The salt tax was repealed in its entirety
Congress agreed to participate in the Second Round Table Conference
Political prisoners not convicted of violence were to be released
Coastal villagers were allowed to make salt for domestic consumption
questions.e: The Pact only allowed salt-making for personal use in coastal villages; the salt tax remained. In return Congress suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement and agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946:
1. It rejected the demand for a separate sovereign Pakistan.
2. It proposed a Union of India limited to defence, foreign affairs and communications.
3. Group C was to comprise Bengal and Punjab.
4. Group A was to comprise the Hindu-majority provinces of Madras, Bombay, United Provinces, Bihar, Central Provinces and Orissa.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Group C was to comprise Bengal and Assam; Group B consisted of Punjab, Sind, NWFP and Baluchistan. The other three statements describe the plan correctly.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q: Which one of the following temples is NOT correctly matched with the dynasty that built it?
questions.e: The Sun Temple at Modhera was built under the Solanki (Chaulukya) dynasty of Gujarat. The Hoysalas built Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania, Indian Art and Culture

questions.q: Which one of the following Ashokan minor rock edict sites explicitly names the king 'Ashoka' in its text, rather than only 'Devanampiya Piyadasi'?
questions.e: The Maski (Karnataka) minor rock edict, along with Gujjara, Nittur and Udegolam, names Ashoka, which confirmed that Devanampiya Piyadasi was Ashoka.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania; Romila Thapar / NCERT Ancient India

questions.q: National income, defined as net national product at factor cost, is equal to
o: GDP at market price minus depreciation minus net indirect taxes
GDP at factor cost plus depreciation
GDP at market price minus depreciation plus net factor income from abroad minus net indirect taxes
GNP at market price plus net indirect taxes
questions.e: Start from GDP at market price, subtract depreciation to get NDP, add net factor income from abroad to get NNP, and subtract net indirect taxes (indirect taxes less subsidies) to move from market prices to factor cost.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the Human Development Index as computed by the UNDP since 2010?
questions.e: Since 2010 the education dimension uses mean and expected years of schooling, replacing adult literacy and gross enrolment ratio. Health uses life expectancy and income uses GNI per capita (PPP).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts.
2. Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.
3. Effective revenue deficit is revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets.
4. A revenue deficit means that the government is borrowing to finance capital formation.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A revenue deficit implies borrowing is financing current consumption (revenue spending), not capital formation, which is why it is considered harmful. Statements 1 to 3 are the standard definitions.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a component of reserve money (high-powered money) in India?
o: Time deposits of the public with commercial banks
questions.e: Reserve money is the RBI's monetary liabilities: currency in circulation, bankers' deposits and other deposits with the RBI. Time deposits with commercial banks form part of broad money M3 but not of reserve money.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Wholesale Price Index does not include services.
2. The Consumer Price Index measures changes in retail prices faced by consumers.
3. India's flexible inflation targeting framework is anchored on the Wholesale Price Index.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The statutory inflation target under the RBI Act is defined on CPI (Combined), not WPI. WPI covers only goods and no services, while CPI reflects retail prices.

questions.q: Under the RBI's liquidity management framework introduced in April 2022, the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate is set
o: at 25 basis points above the policy repo rate
at the same level as the policy repo rate
at 25 basis points below the policy repo rate
at 25 basis points above the Marginal Standing Facility rate
questions.e: The SDF replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor of the liquidity corridor, at repo minus 25 bp, while the MSF rate is repo plus 25 bp. The SDF needs no collateral.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Ch 'Banking'; RBI statement on policy, April 2022

questions.q: Which one of the following is recorded under the current account of India's Balance of Payments?
o: Remittances sent home by Indian workers abroad
Deposits by Non-Resident Indians in Indian banks
questions.e: Remittances are secondary income transfers and fall in the current account. FDI, ECBs and NRI deposits are capital/financial account items.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices is a statutory body.
2. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approves the Minimum Support Prices.
3. The Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane is announced by the Central Government on the recommendation of the CACP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CACP is an attached office of the Agriculture Ministry, not a statutory body. The CCEA approves both MSP and the sugarcane FRP on the basis of CACP's recommendations.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about MGNREGA is NOT correct?
o: Wage and material components are to be in a 60:40 ratio at the Gram Panchayat level
An unemployment allowance is payable if work is not provided within 15 days of application
At least one-third of beneficiaries are to be women
Zila Parishads are the principal authorities for planning and implementing works
questions.e: Gram Panchayats are the principal authorities for planning and implementation, with the Gram Sabha approving works. The other three are provisions of the Act and its Schedules.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Ch 'Poverty and Social Sector'; MGNREGA 2005

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The pyramid of energy in an ecosystem is always upright.
2. The pyramid of biomass can be inverted in an aquatic ecosystem such as the open ocean.
3. The pyramid of numbers is always upright.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Energy is lost as heat at every transfer, so the energy pyramid cannot invert. Biomass can invert where small phytoplankton reproduce quickly but are outweighed by zooplankton, and the numbers pyramid inverts in a single-tree ecosystem with many insects.
questions.h: Energy never flips; numbers and biomass can

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Detritus rich in lignin and chitin decomposes more slowly than detritus rich in nitrogen and sugars.
2. Warm and moist conditions favour decomposition.
3. Anaerobic conditions speed up decomposition.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Temperature and soil moisture are the key climatic controls, and lignin and chitin are resistant substrates. Lack of oxygen slows decomposition, which is why peat and organic-rich waterlogged soils accumulate.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Coral reefs flourish only in clear, shallow tropical waters.
Statement-II: The symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) living in coral tissue need sunlight for photosynthesis.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Reef-building corals get much of their food from zooxanthellae, which photosynthesise, so reefs are confined to the sunlit zone and clear water. Turbid or deep water cuts the light and the reef fails.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. To qualify as a biodiversity hotspot, a region must have at least 1,500 species of vascular plants as endemics.
2. A hotspot must have lost at least 70 percent of its original natural vegetation.
3. The Eastern Ghats is recognised as a biodiversity hotspot in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Norman Myers' criteria, adopted by Conservation International, are the two stated. India's hotspot regions are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).

questions.q: Which one of the following was the first biosphere reserve in India, designated in 1986?
questions.e: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, spread across Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, was the first, and was later included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
International agreement : Main subject
1. Basel Convention : Transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
2. Rotterdam Convention : Prior informed consent for trade in certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides
3. Stockholm Convention : Protection of the ozone layer
4. Minamata Convention : Mercury
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Stockholm Convention (2001) deals with persistent organic pollutants; the ozone layer is protected by the Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Statement-I: Under the Kyoto Protocol, only developed countries listed in Annex I had legally binding emission reduction targets.
Statement-II: The Kyoto Protocol was based on the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because developed countries had contributed most of the historical emissions, the Protocol placed binding commitments only on them while developing countries such as India and China had none in the first commitment period.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about geostationary satellites is NOT correct?
o: They orbit in the equatorial plane
Their orbital period equals Earth's rotation period
They orbit at an altitude of about 36,000 km above the surface
They provide good coverage of the polar regions
questions.e: A satellite fixed over the equator sees the poles only at a very low, grazing angle, so polar coverage is poor. That is why polar and high-latitude services use polar or highly elliptical orbits.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's Mars Orbiter Mission placed a spacecraft in Mars orbit in its first attempt.
2. Aditya-L1 was placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point.
3. Chandrayaan-3 landed on the far side of the Moon.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole on the near side. The MOM entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014 and Aditya-L1 sits at L1, about 1.5 million km from Earth towards the Sun.

questions.q: The Chandrasekhar limit, about 1.4 times the mass of the Sun, is the maximum mass of
o: a neutron star supported by neutron degeneracy pressure
a white dwarf supported by electron degeneracy pressure
a red giant before helium flash
questions.e: Beyond this mass electron degeneracy pressure cannot resist gravity, and the stellar remnant collapses into a neutron star or black hole.

questions.q:
Statement-I: India's three-stage nuclear power programme ultimately aims to use thorium as the main fuel.
Statement-II: India has large reserves of thorium, found in monazite sands, but limited reserves of uranium.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Stage I uses pressurised heavy water reactors on natural uranium, stage II fast breeder reactors using plutonium, and stage III thorium-uranium-233 reactors. The resource position of thorium versus uranium is the reason for this design.

questions.q: In the genetically modified mustard hybrid DMH-11, the barnase and barstar genes are used for
o: hybrid seed production through male sterility and restoration of fertility
questions.e: Barnase makes the female parent line male sterile and barstar in the male parent restores fertility in the hybrid, allowing controlled cross pollination in a self-pollinating crop. The bar gene separately gives herbicide tolerance, and the Bt cry gene gives insect resistance.

questions.q: Under the Patents Act, 1970 as amended, the term of a patent in India is
o: 14 years from the date of grant
20 years from the date of grant
25 years from the date of filing
20 years from the date of filing
questions.e: Following India's TRIPS compliance in 2005 the term is 20 years from the filing date, uniformly for all fields, and renewal fees must be paid yearly.
